title: Relink is out: repair SerializeReference data after a rename in Unity 6
body:
Relink is out: it repairs [SerializeReference] data after you rename a class in Unity 6.

Rename a class, move it to another namespace or assembly, and every [SerializeReference] value of it reads null. The data is still in the files under the old name. Relink scans every scene, prefab and asset, proposes the class each entry belongs to now from the field names Unity kept, and rewrites only the type lines (or writes [MovedFrom] onto the class). Every original is journaled and one click reverts it.

What we measured before shipping:

  • On the demo after a simulated refactor (a case change, a namespace move, three renames and one class split in two), Unity itself loads 3 of 13 spell entries. After Relink: 13 of 13, read in a fresh Unity process.
  • Break the demo, then repair it with Relink: all three files come back byte for byte identical to what Unity originally wrote (sha256 compared).
  • Build machine: RelinkCI.Check exits 0 on the clean demo and 1 after the refactor; RelinkCI.Apply rewrites the 8 confident type lines and exits 1 on the one it will not guess; one line in the map file and it exits 0. 13 of 13 checks by process exit code across 14 Unity processes.
  • Installed from the shipped .unitypackage into a blank Unity 6000.5.7f1 project: 19 files, 0 missing scripts in the demo scene, and 33 of 33 of its own tests passing on the installed bytes.
  • 10,000 asset files with managed references scanned in 14.68 s (12.92 s warm) on a busy shared machine: a sample, not a promise.

Two things we did not expect. A value added through a prefab override is invisible to Unity's own missing type check: it returns false for that instance while the value is gone. And Unity applies [MovedFrom] to a top level reference but not inside a generic argument, so Relink keeps listing those until the assets are rewritten.

Tested on 6000.5.7f1. Text serialized assets only; binary ones are listed, never counted as clean.

Relink on itch.io, $9.99, full C# source, a numbered guide and a demo scene.
